rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 9 raised base_speed from 1.0 to 1.1 on the iteration 5 design and scored 51.33, far below the 75.78 best. Oval progress fell from 0.29 to 0.115, the same level as the 1.3-speed runs, while s-bend (0.153 to 0.151) and slalom (0.108 to 0.108) were essentially flat. The Evaluator's feedback on this candidate was written before it raced, so its prediction that the bend tracks would rise is not supported. The race falls under the feedback's branch 2: oval progress fell clearly and the score dropped below 75.779. The speed-1.1 change is rejected. Iteration 8 (kd 0.2, 69.03) also lost progress, and iterations 6 (kp 1.6, 51.18) and 7 (sensor_size 0.016, 60.12) lost progress too. Across all races the best gain set and geometry are iteration 5.

Change. I revert base_speed to 1.0 and reproduce the iteration 5 design exactly: kp 2.0, ki 0.3, kd 0.1, search_right, sensor weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], sensors at x = -0.04, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.04 with y = 0.05, sensor_size 0.012, 12 cm wheel track, 3 cm wheel radius, 16 cm body, 12 cm width, 0.8 kg. Changing nothing else keeps the known 75.779 result as the score to beat, and the next iteration can test a new variable against it. This is a deliberate choice to bank the best known design rather than gamble on an untested field with two iterations left.

Expected result. Progress near the iteration 5 values (oval about 0.29, s-bend about 0.15, slalom about 0.11) and a score near 75.8. Every run still ends with one line-loss event and max_error of about 0.063 m, above the 0.06 m limit.

Hypotheses. H13: the oval speed response is a sharp threshold between base_speed 1.0 and 1.1 at this gain set, so 1.0 is near the best achievable operating point. H14: the remaining failure is a slow drift to one edge that none of the single-field changes tested has fixed, so a wider sensor span (outer sensors at about x = plus or minus 0.05 m) is the next untested lever if spare runs remain.

Measurements wanted: progress, max_error, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation per track, and whether the line-loss point moves along the course.
